item.title: The Y roll out new body image training program through innovative partnership with The Embrace Collective
item.description: YMCA Victoria will introduce body image training for its early learning and outside school hours care (OSHC) teams through a partnership with The Embrace Collective. Announced on 4 November, the partnership focuses on how adults talk with children about food, movement and their bodies.

item.title: Preschool funding protests grow as services forecast steep losses
item.description: Guardian Childcare and Education is seeking to acquire Mini Masterminds Macquarie Park as the new home for families and their children attending Guardian’s Macquarie Park and Marsfield sites, both of which will be closed in the coming weeks.

item.title: Asking children to name their superpowers puts their voices first
item.description: At Koala Kindy, Fraser Coast Anglican College, our Children’s Week project began with a question: “What is your superpower?” Starting in Term 3, educators spent time with each child exploring their strengths and how they believed those strengths helped others.

item.title: QCCS marks 35th anniversary with extraordinary long service tenure - 100 team members over 10 year mark
item.description: Queensland Childcare Services (QCCS) is marking its 35th anniversary by recognising the educators and team members who have spent more than a decade with the organisation with the provider saying more than 100 employees have worked with QCCS for between 10 and 26 years.

item.title: Education Minister’s meeting completed: Early Learning Commission, CCTV and supervision reforms all on agenda
item.description: The much anticipated third and final Education Ministers meeting of 2026 has now been completed with Education Ministers from across Australia reaching agreements in principle to progress key reforms and changes on several issues central to the early learning sector.

item.title: New rooms, new routines: planning children’s transitions for 2027
item.description: A Sydney-based family day care service is being investigated over suspected Child Care Subsidy claims for care not provided or overstated, according to a joint release involving the Australian Federal Police. Investigators are examining allegedly false attendance claims, inflated care hours and other irregular claiming patterns.

item.title: Rising interest rates: what could affordability pressures mean for children’s access to early learning?
item.description: The Reserve Bank of Australia’s increase in the cash rate to 4.85 per cent brings renewed attention to how families balance family budgets, working hours and early learning costs. The increase of 0.25 percent adds to the financial pressures facing households.

item.title: Exceeding ratings now held by more than half of Little Scholars’ centres
item.description: Nine of Little Scholars School of Early Learning’s 17 Queensland early learning centres are now rated Exceeding the National Quality Standard (NQS), following the most recent assessment at the Karalee’s centres first assessment. The result brings the proportion across the family-owned provider’s centres to approximately 53 per cent.

item.title: Family day care educator earns national recognition after 15 years
item.description: CCA Family Day Care educator Tivana Sando has been named one of four national Educator of the Year finalists in the 2026 Excellence in Family Day Care Awards. The Sydney educator will represent the combined NSW/ACT region when the national winners are announced in Brisbane on 28 November.
